original_question: Classify asymptotically flat black holes in spacetime dimension higher than four and determine whether higher-dimensional black holes satisfy a uniqueness theorem analogous to the four-dimensional Kerr uniqueness results.
target_in_paper: Section 4.2, Problem P9: "Determine the uniqueness of black holes in higher dimensions." The nearby context makes clear that the motivation is the contrast between 4D Kerr uniqueness and the existence of multiple asymptotically flat higher-dimensional vacuum black hole solutions, and it also identifies related subproblems involving analyticity, non-degeneracy, connectedness, and vacuum near-horizon geometries with compact cross-sections. refined_question: In general relativity, for stationary asymptotically flat vacuum black holes in spacetime dimension D > 4, determine whether there is a higher-dimensional analogue of the 4D Schwarzschild/Kerr black-hole uniqueness theorems, after formulating the appropriate higher-dimensional versions of the standard assumptions such as analyticity, non-degeneracy, and connectedness. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))
justification: The nearest official formulation is Problem P9 in Section 4.2, not a broader classification statement. The surrounding text explains that the question is motivated by the failure of naive 4D-style uniqueness in higher dimensions: unlike in 4D, there are multiple asymptotically flat higher-dimensional vacuum black hole solutions. The paper then explicitly points to the higher-dimensional adaptation of analyticity, non-degeneracy, and connectedness as the right precision-enhancing context for the uniqueness problem. Section 3.4 supplies the intended 4D background by describing the Schwarzschild/Kerr uniqueness results and the role of stationary black-hole uniqueness assumptions. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))
